decisions.reason: This classic lever line sits in the core range and costs little to maintain, so the firm will likely keep it despite its lower web visibility since 2020.
The multi-model family carries sunk tooling and catalogue investment that management will want to justify, and weak visibility can still be read as normal specification cycles.

This single design has little invested in it and has not been visible since 2019, which makes it the most exposed, but a fittings maker usually lets such designs run on in the catalogue rather than actively cutting them.
The lever family supports the firm's announced push toward system breadth and embodies investment across several models, so persistence is likely.

The L700 access system is the publicly announced flagship of the firm's digital building direction with heavy investment behind it, so management will stick with it and blame any weakness on temporary market factors.
